Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap: Acme Corp TCO discussion & next steps

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we have alignment. High-level notes below; attaching a TCO estimate and a one-pager for procurement.

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-token spend on peak chat workloads (esp. system prompts + long context).
- Burstiness: peak windows where latency spikes and cost is unpredictable.
- Need to keep customer PII in a VPC / strict data controls for compliance.

Goals you’re trying to hit (Q3):
- Reduce per-inference unit cost by ~30% while preserving quality for user-facing chat.
- Maintain 99.9% availability for critical flows; burst tolerance during peak hours.
- Make procurement-friendly cost case (annualized TCO) for budget owners.

TCO levers we discussed (how Redwood helps):
1) Model variant + quantization mix — run cheaper int8/8-bit quantized variants for non-core prompts and keep higher-precision models for critical system messages.
2) Batching + continuous KV cache — reduce redundant token generation by caching common prefixes and batching requests in 50–200ms windows where latency SLO allows. This is our biggest immediate cost saver for bursty traffic.
3) Smart routing + reserved capacity — combine Dedicated capacity for steady baseline throughput and Hosted fallback for unpredictable spikes to reduce over-provisioning.
4) Prompt engineering + system message consolidation — small prompt changes that reduce average context length can shrink token counts by 10–20%.

Attached: acme-tco-estimate-20270630.xlsx (breakdown by token cost, batch savings, reserved vs hosted), redwood-pricing-onepager.pdf.

Initial estimate (ballpark):
- Current monthly token spend (as discussed): ~$25k
- Expected monthly after optimization (batching + quant + routing): ~$16k–$18k (~28–36% savings)
- Estimated first-year net savings (annualized incl. reserved commit discount): $60k–$85k depending on commit level.

Suggested next steps:
1) You share last 30 days of aggregate request/usage patterns (no PII) so we can run the estimator against real traffic.
2) Technical deep-dive with Rafael to align on batching thresholds, KV cache patterns, and VPC/network requirements (30–45 minutes).
3) Procurement one-pager for your finance team; I’ve attached a draft—happy to trim it to procurement format.
4) If agreed, spin up a 30-day pilot on Dedicated baseline + hosted burst (pilot pricing outlined in the attached sheet).

Can you confirm: (a) budget target for this initiative (you mentioned ~$200k ARR as a ballpark?), and (b) who from procurement should I include on the next email?

Thanks again — I’ll wait for the usage export and will schedule Rafael after you confirm logistics.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
